subject: English
title: Priya and Rohan's Market Adventure
hook: Learn to read and understand short stories about everyday friends and families.

slides.title: Reading Comprehension
slides.storyContext: Priya and Rohan learn to read and understand stories about people, places, and fun things.

slides.title: At the Market
slides.storyContext: Priya and Rohan go to the market with Priya's mama. They see colourful fruits, vegetables, and happy shopkeepers. Read along as they discover new words and ideas.

slides.title: Who, What, and Where?

points.label: Who
points.text: Identify the characters in the story — people, animals, or objects that do things.

points.label: What
points.text: Find out what happens — the action or event in the story.

points.label: Where
points.text: Notice where the story takes place — home, school, market, park.

example.problem: Story: Priya sees red apples at the market. Question: Where does Priya see the apples?
example.solution: Answer: At the market.

slides.inSimpleWords: When we read, we ask: Who is in the story? What do they do? Where does it happen?

slides.title: Picture and Words Work Together

points.text: Look at pictures in the book to help you understand the story.
Pictures show you what the words mean.
Pictures make stories more fun and clear.

example.problem: You see a picture of a child eating mango. The words say: 'Aman eats a mango.' What does Aman eat?
example.solution: Answer: A mango. The picture helps you know this.

slides.inSimpleWords: Pictures are like helpers that show you what the story is about.

slides.title: Reading Order Words

points.text: First: the beginning of the story.
Next: what happens in the middle.
Last: how the story ends.

example.problem: Story: First, Rohan wakes up. Next, he eats breakfast. Last, he goes to school. What does Rohan do first?
example.solution: Answer: Rohan wakes up first.

slides.inSimpleWords: Stories happen in order: first, next, last. This order helps us understand what happened when.

slides.title: Feeling Words in Stories

points.text: Happy, sad, scared, surprised — these are feelings.
Stories tell us how characters feel.
We can feel the same way when we read.

example.problem: Story: Priya finds her lost toy. She smiles and jumps. How does Priya feel?
example.solution: Answer: Priya is happy. We know because she smiles and jumps.

slides.inSimpleWords: When we read, we notice how the people in the story feel — happy, sad, or scared.

slides.title: Find the Main Idea

points.text: The main idea is the big thing the story is about.
It is not one small detail — it is what the whole story teaches.
Ask: What is this story really telling me?

example.problem: Story: Rohan helps his friend. He picks up her books. He shares his lunch. What is this story really about?
example.solution: Answer: The story is about helping a friend. That is the main idea.

slides.inSimpleWords: The main idea is the big message of the story, not just one small thing that happened.

slides.title: Read This Short Story
slides.storyContext: Read this real story and find the answers.

example.problem: Anya goes to her grandmother's house. She sees a garden with red flowers and green plants. Her grandmother is watering the plants. 'Come, Anya,' says Grandmother. 'Let us water the flowers together.' Anya is happy. She helps water the plants.
example.solution: Questions: 1) Who is the main character? Answer: Anya. 2) Where is she? Answer: At her grandmother's house. 3) What does she do? Answer: She waters plants with her grandmother. 4) How does Anya feel? Answer: Happy.

slides.title: Your Turn to Read and Answer
slides.storyContext: Read this story and find the answers in your workbook.

example.problem: Ravi and his sister Diya play cricket in the park. Diya hits the ball very far. 'Wow!' says Ravi. 'You are good!' Diya laughs. They play until the sun goes down. Then they go home happy and tired.
example.solution: 1) Who are the characters? Answer: Ravi and Diya. 2) What do they do? Answer: They play cricket. 3) Where do they play? Answer: In the park. 4) How do they feel at the end? Answer: Happy and tired.

slides.title: What We Learned Today

points.text: Read stories about people, places, and things we know.
Ask Who, What, and Where to understand the story.
Pictures help us understand words.
Stories happen in order: first, next, last.
Notice feelings: happy, sad, scared.
Find the main idea — what is the story really about?

slides.inSimpleWords: Good readers ask questions and think about what they read. You are becoming a great reader!

subject: English
title: Arjun's Sentence Adventures
hook: Write simple sentences about friends, families, and fun things you love.

slides.title: Simple Writing
slides.storyContext: Arjun learns to write simple, clear sentences about his life and the people he loves.

slides.title: Arjun Wants to Write
slides.storyContext: Arjun goes to Teacher Aunty. 'I want to write a story,' he says. 'But how do I start?' Teacher Aunty smiles. 'We will make it easy. First, we write simple sentences.'

slides.title: A Sentence Has a Subject and an Action

points.label: Subject
points.text: The person or thing the sentence is about (who or what).

points.label: Action
points.text: What the subject does (the verb).

example.problem: Write a sentence about Saya doing something. Use: Saya + an action.
example.solution: Saya plays football. (Subject: Saya. Action: plays.)

slides.inSimpleWords: Every sentence needs someone or something (the subject) and something they do (the action).

slides.title: Use Capital Letters and Full Stops

points.text: Start every sentence with a capital letter.
End every sentence with a full stop (.).
Capital letters show that a sentence is starting.

example.problem: Fix this: arjun is a good boy. Answer: Arjun is a good boy.
example.solution: We start with a capital A. We end with a full stop. Now it is correct!

slides.inSimpleWords: Sentences start big (capital letter) and end with a dot (full stop).

slides.title: Describing Words Make Sentences Better

points.text: Describing words tell us more about nouns.
Examples: big, small, red, happy, quick, slow, beautiful.
Describing words help readers picture the story.

example.problem: Sentence: Saya has an apple. Make it better with a describing word.
example.solution: Saya has a red apple. Or: Saya has a big apple. The describing word makes it clearer!

slides.inSimpleWords: Describing words help us see and feel the story better. They paint a picture with words.

slides.title: Write About Things You Know

points.text: Write about your family, friends, home, school.
Write about things you do every day.
Write about your feelings and your favourite things.

example.problem: Write a sentence about your favourite food from home.
example.solution: My mother makes tasty dal and rice. Or: I like sweet ladoos. Write what you really know and like!

slides.inSimpleWords: The best stories come from your own life. Write what you know.

slides.title: Sentences Tell Complete Thoughts

points.text: A sentence is a complete thought. It makes sense on its own.
Incomplete: 'The big dog.' (What about the dog?)
Complete: 'The big dog runs fast.' (Now we know what it does.)

example.problem: Is this a complete sentence? 'Ravi in the garden.' Answer: No. Make it complete.
example.solution: Ravi plays in the garden. Now it is complete and makes sense.

slides.inSimpleWords: A good sentence tells a complete thought. Read it and ask: Does it make sense?

slides.title: Write Your Own Sentences
slides.storyContext: Here are real sentence examples about friends and school.

example.problem: Write three sentences about your best friend or your school day.
example.solution: Example 1: My friend Isha is kind and smart. Example 2: We play together in the park. Example 3: I like being with Isha.

slides.title: Write a Short Paragraph
slides.storyContext: Now write 3–4 simple sentences about something you did today.

example.problem: Write a short paragraph: What did you do today? Use complete sentences. Start with capital letters. End with full stops.
example.solution: Example: Today I went to school. My teacher taught us about animals. I drew a picture of a tiger. Then I played with my friends. This is a short paragraph — 4 complete sentences about one day.

slides.title: Writing Tips to Remember

points.text: A sentence has a subject (who or what) and an action (what they do).
Start with a capital letter. End with a full stop.
Use describing words to paint a picture.
Write about things you know and love.
Make sure your sentence is complete and makes sense.
Be proud of your writing!

slides.inSimpleWords: You are a writer now! Write simple, clear sentences about your life. Every day, you will get better.

subject: English
title: Maya's Word Treasure Hunt
hook: Discover new words and learn what they mean through fun stories and pictures.

slides.title: Words and Meanings
slides.storyContext: Maya and Vikram hunt for new words. Grandmother teaches them real, everyday words from stories.

slides.title: The Word Treasure Hunt Begins
slides.storyContext: Maya and Vikram sit with Grandmother in the garden. 'Grandmother, can you teach us new words?' asks Maya. Grandmother nods. 'Of course! The world is full of beautiful words. Let us find them together.'

slides.title: Every Word Has a Meaning

points.text: A word is a sound or group of letters that stands for something.
The meaning is what the word tells us.
Pictures, stories, and examples help us learn meanings.

example.problem: Word: GARDEN. What does garden mean?
example.solution: A garden is a place where plants and flowers grow. It can have vegetables, flowers, or trees. Grandmother's garden has bright flowers.

slides.inSimpleWords: A word is like a name for something. The meaning tells us what that something is.

slides.title: Rhyming Words Sound the Same at the End

points.text: Rhyming words end with the same sound.
Examples: cat and hat, run and fun, day and play.
Rhymes make stories fun to read and remember.

example.problem: Find a word that rhymes with 'ball'. Answer choices: wall, food, tree.
example.solution: Answer: wall. Ball and wall rhyme because they end with the same sound: -all.

slides.inSimpleWords: Rhyming words are like sound friends. They sound alike at the end.

slides.title: Opposite Words

points.label: Opposites
points.text: Words that mean completely different things.
Examples: big and small, hot and cold, happy and sad.
Opposites help us describe things better.

example.problem: Opposite of 'tall'. Answer choices: short, fast, red.
example.solution: Answer: short. Tall and short are opposites. Tall means big up-down. Short means not big up-down.

slides.inSimpleWords: Opposite words are like two ends of a line. They mean different things.

slides.title: Words That Sound the Same But Mean Different Things

points.text: Some words sound the same but mean different things.
Example: 'sun' (in the sky) and 'son' (a boy child). Both sound like 'sun'.
We learn which is which from the sentence around it.

example.problem: Vikram sees the sun. The sun is bright and warm. Does this 'sun' mean a boy child? Answer: No.
example.solution: 'Sun' here means the star in the sky, not a boy child (son). The sentence tells us it is bright and warm. That helps us know which word it is.

slides.inSimpleWords: Some words sound the same but mean different things. The sentence helps us know which one.

slides.title: New Words From Stories

points.text: When you read, you find new words you do not know.
Look at the story and pictures for clues.
Ask yourself: 'What does this word do in the story?'

example.problem: Story: 'The merchant sold silk in the market.' What might 'merchant' mean?
example.solution: A merchant is a person who sells things. The story says the merchant sold silk in the market. We learned the meaning from the story!

slides.inSimpleWords: When you meet a new word, look at the story for clues. The story helps you understand.

slides.title: Real Words From Everyday Life
slides.storyContext: Here are real words Maya and Vikram learned from Grandmother.

example.problem: Learn these words: FESTIVAL (a big celebration with music and food), MONSOON (season of heavy rain), BAZAAR (a busy market), LANTERN (a light that can move).
example.solution: Festival: Diwali is a big festival with lights and sweets. Monsoon: In monsoon, it rains hard for many days. Bazaar: We buy vegetables in the bazaar. Lantern: Grandmother lit a lantern when the lights went out.

slides.title: Find the Meaning
slides.storyContext: Read and find the right meaning.

example.problem: Word: BRAVE. Choose the meaning: (1) scared and worried, (2) not scared and facing danger, (3) alone and sad. What is the meaning of BRAVE?
example.solution: Answer: (2) not scared and facing danger. Vikram is brave when he helps his friend even when he is worried. Brave means you do something even if it is hard.

slides.title: Words Are Everywhere

points.text: Every word has a meaning that tells us what it is.
Rhyming words sound the same at the end.
Opposite words mean different things.
Some words sound the same but mean different things.
Stories and pictures help us learn new word meanings.
Keep learning new words every day!

slides.inSimpleWords: Words are treasures. The more words you know, the more stories you can read and the more you can write.
